messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: continuous-batcher-usw2-pool — 99th latency > 5s for 3m, error spike, paging eng-oncall
alyssa: ack, i'm on it. pulling dashboards and checking recent deploys.
marco: oncall handover note — i was running a canary push to dedicated-pool-usw2 ~5m ago (config change to batching strategy). will list exact change shortly.
jordan: grabbing logs from batcher pods. initial look shows a lot of inflight microbatches stuck in "prefetch-wait" and persistent KV cache misses.
kevin: i'm with customers page — asking support to surface any customer-facing errors. @support_agent can you confirm errors?
support_agent: two enterprise customers reported slow responses and timeouts for their streaming endpoints starting ~10:02 UTC. no 5xx spike, mostly 504 from client side.
alyssa: ok — timeline: deploy at 10:00 UTC, alerts started at 10:02 UTC. sounds like edge-case where the new batching algo increases head-of-line waiting under heavy concurrency (queue-swell).
marco: change was small: switched continuous_batching.mode from "auto-window" to "adaptive-rise" and set microbatch_cap: 6.
jordan: logs snippet from batcher-7f6c:
```
I0321 10:03:05 batcher.cpp:452] enqueue request id=0x7f9, size=128
I0321 10:03:07 batcher.cpp:498] waiting for microbatch fill: current=5 cap=6
W0321 10:03:07 kv_cache.cpp:213] eviction pressure high: active_keys=1.2M, free_slots=120
E0321 10:03:08 router.cpp:340] request timeout after 5000ms
```
alyssa: kv cache eviction pressure + higher microbatch cap = longer head waits. that lines up with queueing + jitter amplifying latency.
kevin: immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce microbatch_cap to 2 2) enable aggressive eviction-throttle 3) rollback canary if needed. who can flip these now?
jordan: i can patch the config for the canary pods. patching via k8s: `kubectl -n inference patch cm continuous-batcher --patch '...` (i'm running the exact patch now).
marco: i'll prepare a quick hotfix config:
```
batcher:
  microbatch_cap: 2
  jitter_ms: 10
  prefetch_limit: 32
kv_cache:
  eviction_throttle: true
  throttle_threshold: 0.75
```
alyssa: thanks. also start a controlled rollout: apply to 10% nodes in pool, watch p99 and error rate for 2m, then expand. set SLO guard rails: if p99 < 1s and error rate drops, proceed.
ops-bot: deploy job started: rollout/continuous-batcher-hotfix -> 10% target (5 pods). Job ID: dj-2955-hotfix-1
marco: hotfix applied to 5 pods. monitoring...
jordan: immediate telemetry: p99 dropped to ~900ms on patched pods, p95 ~180ms. unpatched pods still at p99 ~5.2s.
support_agent: customer thread updated: told customers we're mitigating and expect improvement in next 5-10m. they acknowledged.
kevin: good. let's keep customers informed. Alyssa, you want to coordinate handoff?
alyssa: yes — i'll keep the page for 15 min; if stable, handoff to marco for overnight. need a short postmortem stub after.
marco: after 6m expansion to 50% showed continued improvement, expanding to 100% now.
jordan: rolling to remaining pods. commands used:
```
kubectl -n inference set env ds/continuous-batcher MICROBATCH_CAP=2
kubectl -n inference rollout restart ds/continuous-batcher
```
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Hotfix rollout progressing — 100% patched at 10:22 UTC. p99 cluster-wide now 820ms, errors down 78%.
alyssa: verifying customer impact logs; support_agent can you confirm any lingering customer errors after 10:25?
support_agent: only 1 small client reported intermittent timeouts earlier, cleared after 10:26. no new reports.
kevin: tally of actions: patched microbatch cap down, reduced jitter window, enabled eviction throttle, canary -> full rollout. no rollback needed.
sre_lead: capture root cause: the new adaptive-rise mode increases per-request waiting to try to reach larger batches. under high concurrency with KV cache thrashing this turned into head-of-line blocking and eviction cascade. chronology in PM.
marco: logging note — add a guard in batcher that rejects waiting if queue latency > 250ms and force microbatch flush. will open ticket.
alyssa: opening incident doc now and scheduling 1-hour postmortem tomorrow. short notes:
- Severity: P2 (customer impact, mitigated)
- Affected: dedicated-pool-usw2 (all tenants on that pool)
- Root cause: batching algorithm change + high KV eviction pressure -> queueing/cliff
- Mitigation: microbatch cap reduced, eviction_throttle enabled, full rollout
- Next steps: add guard, add perf test for concurrency wave, improve canary checks, add synthetic customer probes during canary.
ops-bot: incident doc created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2955 (placeholder)
kevin: handing the incident to @marco for overnight watch. marco you'll take action if p99 > 2s or errors > 5% baseline?
marco: yes, i'll keep a 2h watch and escalate to sre_lead if it reappears.
alyssa: handing off now — leaving pager to marco. logging handoff: "oncall -> marco at 10:30 UTC, stable after hotfix rollout" :white_check_mark:
marco: ack, thanks. I'll follow up with a short postmortem and the PR for the guard.
incident-bot: :pager: Handoff recorded: previous_oncall=alyssa, new_oncall=marco, handoff_ts=2955554700
